resolution.summary: The District Attorney's Office dismissed the misdemeanor case; as part of the dismissal Esparza made a statement admitting he was angry at Sloan, ABC30 reported.

citations.quote: The Fresno County District Attorney's Office has dismissed a misdemeanor attempted extortion case against Fresno City Council President Nelson Esparza.
As part of the case being dropped, Esparza had to make an apologetic statement, in which he admitted he was angry at Sloan.

response.summary: Esparza said in July 2022 that he was not guilty; when the case was dismissed he read a court statement saying his words could have implied a threat to fire Sloan but were misunderstood, and said he came out of the process as he entered it, "a free and innocent man".

citations.quote: Nelson Esparza said he's not going anywhere and he's not guilty.
In Monday’s courtroom statement, Esparza admitted his words could have implied a threat to fire Sloan, but he said his statements were misunderstood.
"I came into this process as a free and innocent man and am coming out of the process the same way.

items.summary: ABC30 reported that Esparza was accused of threatening to fire then-City Attorney Doug Sloan unless Sloan worked exclusively for Esparza and the council majority; a judge reduced the felony charge to a misdemeanor in November 2022, and the Fresno County District Attorney's Office dismissed the case, KVPR and ABC30 reported.
items.title: Attempted extortion charge filed in 2022 and dismissed

citations.quote: Esparza was accused of threatening to fire then-City Attorney Doug Sloan, unless Sloan worked exclusively for Esparza and the council majority.
In November, a judge decided there was enough evidence for a trial but reduced the felony attempted extortion charge to a misdemeanor.

The Fresno County District Attorney’s office dismissed an attempted extortion charge this week against Fresno City Council President Nelson Esparza, ending a months-long legal dispute involving the former city attorney.
